const r = await tools.exec_command({cmd:"python3 - <<'PY'
import json
p='docs/quality/summary-qa/root/2026-11-05-batch-002957/expanded-iteration-12/reader-b.json'
rows=[
('Q01','Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle','**Rule (2.5):** A player rules a clearing with more total **warriors plus buildings** than each other player. Tokens and pawns do not contribute. Ordinary ties mean nobody rules. Eyrie rule a tie for most if they have at least one Eyrie piece there. Vagabond cannot rule or stop someone else ruling.','Count warriors and buildings only. A strict plurality rules; an ordinary tie means no one rules. Eyrie wins a tie for most when it has at least one Eyrie piece there. Tokens and pawns do not count, and the Vagabond neither rules nor prevents another player from ruling.'),
('Q02','Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle','**Move (4.2):** Take any positive number of your warriors/pawns from one clearing along a linking path to an adjacent clearing. You must rule origin or destination or both. Recheck rule for each move. You may move the same pieces repeatedly, including on multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly treats them as paths.','A normal move takes at least one of your warriors or pawns between adjacent clearings along a linking path, and you must rule the origin, destination, or both. Recheck rule for each move. The same pieces may move repeatedly, including in multiple moves within one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly says otherwise.'),
('Q03','Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle','**Battle (4.3):** Choose a clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy there as defender. **Battle does not require you to rule the clearing.** Resolve these six steps:\n\n1. **Ambush:** Defender may play one ambush matching clearing (birds are wild). Attacker may foil it with a matching ambush. Defender\'s card is discarded; a foiled ambush deals no hits. Otherwise defender immediately deals two hits, then discards ambush. If no attacking warriors or pawns remain, battle ends immediately. Ambush hits are not limited by defending warriors.\n2. **Before-roll effects:** Resolve applicable effects; attacker chooses order if both have them.\n3. **Roll:** Higher die is attacker\'s rolled hits, lower defender\'s; equal dice give equal results. Each side\'s rolled hits are capped by its own warriors in battle. Alliance defending reverses the dice; Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead of warriors.\n4. **After-roll effects:** Resolve effects affecting battle that do not say “before rolling”; attacker chooses order if both have them.\n5. **Count hits:** Add extra hits (uncapped by warriors), subtract ignored hits. If defender has no warriors, attacker deals one extra hit for **defenseless**; Vagabond is instead defenseless if it has no undamaged swords.\n6. **Deal hits:** Each hit removes one opposing piece. The side taking hits chooses its own removal order, but **all its warriors must be removed before its buildings/tokens**. It also chooses order of effects triggered by its pieces\' removal. Both sides deal their counted hits; losing warriors does not retroactively change the rolled cap. Whoever removes an enemy building/token scores **one VP each**, even while defending and even outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage instead.','Battle proceeds Ambush, before-roll effects, roll, after-roll effects, count hits, then deal hits. The defender may ambush with a matching card (bird wild); attacker can foil with a matching ambush, discarding the defender’s card and preventing hits. Otherwise ambush deals two immediate hits, uncapped by warriors; if no attacking warriors/pawns remain, battle ends. Higher die gives attacker hits, lower die defender hits (equal dice equal hits), capped by each side’s warriors; Alliance defending reverses dice and Vagabond uses undamaged swords. Add extra hits and subtract ignored hits; a defender with no warriors is defenseless (Vagabond instead needs no undamaged swords), giving attacker one extra hit. Each hit removes one enemy piece; the hit side orders removals but must remove all its warriors before buildings/tokens, and orders its removal-triggered effects. Both sides deal counted hits regardless of warriors subsequently lost. Removing an enemy building/token scores its remover one VP each, including a defender; Vagabond takes hits as item damage.'),
('Q04','Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle','**Craft (4.1):** **Every crafting piece gets its suit from the clearing containing it.** The card\'s **bottom-left crafting icons** require pieces of those clearing suits; the card\'s own suit does not define the cost. Craft a card from hand when your faction permits.\n\n**Personal duplicate check:** Only an identical persistent effect **in your own play area** prevents you from crafting that effect again. Other players\' copies do not count for this duplicate restriction.\n\n- **Marquise, Eyrie and Alliance cost:** For **each icon**, activate **one workshop, roost or sympathy in a clearing matching that icon\'s suit**, respectively. A crafting piece gets its suit from its clearing. Combine eligible pieces as needed, but **each piece may activate only once per turn**.\n- **Immediate effect (paper box):** resolve, then discard the **crafting card**. An item card requires the corresponding **item token** in the map supply, or it cannot be crafted.','Craft a card from hand by meeting each bottom-left icon with a crafting piece whose suit comes from its clearing: Marquise workshops, Eyrie roosts, Alliance sympathy; each piece activates once per turn. (Vagabond has its separate repeat-use rule.) Only an identical persistent effect already in your own play area bars crafting it again; another player’s copy does not. An item card cannot be crafted if its matching map-supply token is absent.'),
('Q05','Scoring / Victory Conditions — Dominance','**Dominance (3.3):** In own Daylight at **at least 10 VP**, activate a dominance card from hand into play area; remove score marker and stop scoring VP. Cannot remove/replace activated card. At **start of own Birdsong**, win if ruling **three clearings of matching mouse/rabbit/fox suit**, or for **bird dominance, two diagonally opposite corner clearings**. Meeting condition earlier does not immediately win.','In your Daylight, at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from hand, put it in your play area, remove your score marker, and stop scoring VP. You cannot remove or replace it. At the start of your Birdsong, mouse/rabbit/fox dominance wins if you rule three clearings of that suit; bird dominance wins if you rule two diagonally opposite corner clearings. Meeting the condition earlier does not win immediately.'),
('Q06','Scoring / Victory Conditions — Dominance','**Dominance (3.3):** ... Whenever one would enter discard, put it near map available instead. During own Daylight, spend matching card to take available dominance into hand. Available **bird dominance remains bird**, so payment must be bird; a bird hand card can pay for non-bird dominance. Activation and taking are separate, neither requires a faction action allowance.','A dominance card spent for suit goes near the map as available instead of into discard. During your Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance card into hand. Bird dominance stays bird and requires a bird card to take; a bird card can pay for a non-bird dominance. Taking and activating are separate and use no faction action allowance.'),
('Q07','Setup','3. With two players, remove all four dominance cards. Shuffle shared deck; each player draws **three cards**.\n4. **Ruins and items:** Cover the four R building slots with ruins. The separate map item supply is **2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, 2 coins**. Keep the four R-marked ruin items separate from this supply: only Vagabond faction setup hides one each of its R-marked bag, boot, hammer and sword beneath the four ruins, **one item beneath each ruin**. During that Vagabond setup, shuffle the ruin/item stacks and return each to an empty R ruin slot, keeping item identities hidden. Without a Vagabond, ruins contain no items.\n7. Set up factions in their letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond. Setup order is distinct from turn order.','For two players, remove all four dominance cards, shuffle the shared deck, and deal each player three cards. Cover four R slots with ruins. The separate map supply has 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, and 2 coins. Only if Vagabond is present, its setup hides one R-marked bag, boot, hammer, and sword, one beneath each ruin; shuffle stacks and return them to empty R slots with identities hidden. Without Vagabond, ruins contain no items. Faction setup order is Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond.'),
('Q08','Marquise de Cat — Keep and Field Hospitals','**Keep:** Only Marquise may **place** pieces in its clearing; other players may **move** pieces into it. The keep cannot be placed again if removed. **Field Hospitals:** Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the keep clearing instead of supply. This can apply outside battle. Without a keep there is no destination for hospitals.','Only Marquise may place pieces in the Keep clearing, though others may move pieces there. If removed, the Keep cannot be placed again. Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one matching-suit card to place them in the Keep clearing instead of supply, even outside battle. Field Hospitals have no destination if the Keep is gone.'),
('Q09','Marquise de Cat — Daylight','**Daylight:** First craft with workshops. Then take **up to three actions**, plus **one per bird card spent outside an action**, in any order and number except Recruit\'s limit:\n- **Battle:** One battle.\n- **March:** Up to two moves; either may use the same or different warriors. Do not interrupt the compound action to spend a bird card or take another action.\n- **Recruit:** One warrior at **each recruiter**; only **once per turn**. If supply cannot fill all recruiters, place maximum available, choosing among eligible recruiters.\n- **Overwork:** Spend a card matching a sawmill\'s clearing to place one wood there.','First craft with workshops, then take up to three actions plus one action for each bird card spent outside an action. Actions may be ordered/repeated except Recruit, which is once per turn. A Battle is one battle. March is up to two moves, using same or different warriors; it is one compound action and cannot be interrupted to spend a bird card or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill clearing to place one wood there.'),
('Q10','Marquise de Cat — Build','- **Build:** Choose a clearing you rule with open slot and choose building type. Take the leftmost building of that type. Pay cost shown atop its column by removing that many wood from the target clearing or from other ruled clearings linked to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place building; score VP on uncovered space. You cannot build without full wood cost, the building and legal slot.','To Build, choose a clearing you rule with an open slot and a building type. Take that type’s leftmost building on its track. Pay the column’s cost using wood in the target clearing or in other ruled clearings connected to it by an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place it and score the VP uncovered on its track. Full wood cost, available building, and legal slot are all required.'),
('Q11','Eyrie Dynasties — Birdsong','**Birdsong, in order:**\n1. **Emergency Orders:** If hand empty, draw one.\n2. **Add to Decree:** Must add one or two hand cards, **at most one added bird card**. Each goes to any column; columns have no size limit.\n3. **A New Roost:** If no roosts on map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors **where all these pieces can be placed**.','First, if your hand is empty, draw one card. Then add one or two hand cards to any Decree columns (no column size limit), with at most one of the added cards a bird. If no roost is on the map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors among clearings where all four pieces can legally be placed.'),
('Q12','Eyrie Dynasties — Daylight, Decree','**Daylight — resolve the Decree:** Craft using roosts first, then resolve **every Decree card**, column by column **Recruit → Move → Battle → Build**. Within one column choose card order freely. Bird is wild. **If any required action cannot be fully completed, immediately enter Turmoil: you cannot skip the card or continue other columns.** Each card requires:\n| Decree column | Match the card\'s suit to | Required procedure for one card |\n| Recruit | Clearing with a roost | Place **one warrior at one chosen roost** there; Charismatic must instead place **two warriors** there |\n| Move | Origin clearing | Move **at least one warrior**, obeying ordinary path and rule requirements |\n| Battle | Clearing of battle | Initiate a battle there with Eyrie warriors and an enemy |\n| Build | Target clearing | Place one roost in a clearing you rule, with an open slot and **no roost already there**','In Daylight craft with roosts first, then resolve every Decree card in column order Recruit, Move, Battle, Build; choose card order within a column, and bird is wild. Recruit suit matches a roost clearing and places one warrior at one chosen roost (Charismatic places two); Move suit matches the origin and requires at least one warrior move obeying normal path/rule rules; Battle suit matches the battle clearing and requires battle by Eyrie warriors against an enemy; Build suit matches target and places a roost where Eyrie rules, a slot is open, and no roost already exists. If any action cannot be fully completed, immediately Turmoil; do not skip it or continue.'),
('Q13','Eyrie Dynasties — Turmoil','**Turmoil, in order:** Lose one VP per bird Decree card **including both Loyal Viziers**; discard every Decree card except Viziers; flip current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement. If none face up, flip all leaders face up before choosing. Retuck Viziers in new leader\'s columns. End Daylight and proceed to the full normal Evening: **score the roost track, draw one plus uncovered bonuses, then discard to five**. **Turmoil does not remove your map warriors or buildings.**','In Turmoil lose 1 VP for every bird Decree card, including both Viziers; discard all Decree cards except Viziers; flip current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement (if none, turn all leaders face up first); retuck Viziers in the new leader’s columns. Daylight ends, then normal Evening still scores the roost track, draws one plus uncovered bonuses, and discards to five. Map warriors and buildings remain.'),
('Q14','Woodland Alliance — Outrage','**Outrage:** Each time another player **removes sympathy** or **moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing**, that player adds one matching hand card (birds count) to Supporters. Moving a group costs one card per affected move, rather than one per warrior. If no matching cards including birds, show hand to Alliance, then Alliance draws one deck card into Supporters. **If Supporters is full, discard the incoming Outrage card; payment or the no-match draw still occurs.** Merely battling there is not a trigger unless sympathy is removed; placing warriors there and moving only Vagabond pawn do not trigger it.','Outrage triggers when another player removes sympathy or moves warriors into a sympathetic clearing. That player adds one matching hand card (bird wild) per affected move, not per warrior. If they have no matching card including birds, show their hand to Alliance and Alliance draws a deck card into Supporters. If Supporters is full, discard the incoming card, but the payment or draw still occurs. Battle alone triggers only if sympathy is removed. Placing warriors and moving only the Vagabond pawn do not trigger it.'),
('Q15','Woodland Alliance — Birdsong','**Birdsong:** Both Revolt and Spread Sympathy take place **during Birdsong**. Complete **all Revolts before starting any Spread Sympathy**; each may be performed any number of times. **For both actions, every supporter spent must match the target clearing; birds are wild.** Once spreading starts, you cannot return to Revolt this Birdsong, so newly spread sympathy cannot support a same-Birdsong Revolt:\n- **Revolt:** Choose sympathetic clearing without a base, matching a base still on your board. Spend **two matching supporters**. **Remove all enemy pieces there and score one VP per enemy building/token removed**; then place matching base. Place warriors there equal to number of sympathetic clearings matching the base\'s printed suit (including revolt clearing), and one warrior in Officers box. Score normal VP for removed enemy buildings/tokens. Resolve the effect even if a prompted placement cannot be completed: place the maximum possible, without adding a base-placement prerequisite. Enemy Vagabond damages three items instead of being removed.\n- **Spread Sympathy:** Choose unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy; if no sympathy anywhere, choose any clearing. Spend matching supporters shown above next sympathy token. **Martial Law:** add one matching supporter if chosen clearing has at least three warriors of **one other player**. Place token and score uncovered space. Only one sympathy per clearing. Keep\'s placement ban still applies.','Both actions occur in Birdsong; finish every Revolt before beginning Spread Sympathy, and each can be done any number of times. Every supporter paid must match the target (birds wild). Revolt targets sympathy without a base and a clearing matching a base still on the Alliance board; pay two supporters, remove all enemy pieces, score 1 VP per enemy building/token, place the matching base, warriors equal to matching-suit sympathy count (including that clearing), and one officer. Maximize placements if supply prevents completion; Vagabond instead damages three items. Spread Sympathy targets an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path (any clearing if none is sympathetic), pays the cost displayed above the next sympathy space, plus one matching supporter under Martial Law if one other player has at least three warriors there. Place one token and score its uncovered VP; one sympathy per clearing and the Keep placement ban applies. Once spreading begins you cannot return to Revolt that Birdsong.'),
('Q16','Woodland Alliance — Daylight / Losing a base','**Losing a base:** Discard all supporters matching its clearing **including birds**, remove half officers **rounded up**. If no bases remain, discard excess supporters down to five. Do this whenever a base is removed.\n\n**Daylight:** Any order and number:\n- **Mobilize:** Add one hand card to Supporters. With no base on map, keep at most five supporters and discard incoming overflow; with any base, the stack has no cap.\n- **Train during Daylight:** Spend a **hand card** matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in Officers box. Supporters cannot pay Train. Each officer allows one Evening military operation; taking operations does not consume officers.\n\nOrganize removes one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing; places sympathy there; scores uncovered VP.','Train in Daylight by spending a hand card matching a clearing with a base to move one supply warrior into Officers; Supporters cannot pay. Each officer permits one Evening military operation and is not consumed by taking it. Organize is an operation: remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, place sympathy there, and score its uncovered VP. Losing a base discards supporters matching its clearing including birds, removes half officers rounded up, and, if no base remains, discards supporters down to five.'),
('Q17','Vagabond — Birdsong / Daylight / Evening','**Birdsong:**\n1. **Refresh:** First count tea **already face up on Refresh track**; flip two exhausted items face up per counted tea, then three more exhausted items. Tea refreshed during this step gives no extra refresh this step. Refreshing changes face, not damaged status.\n2. **Slip (optional):** Move to an adjacent clearing or forest, exhausting **no boots**, even into hostile warriors. Ignore all effects preventing movement **out of** a clearing. **Forest adjacency for Slip:** a forest is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path, and to forests separated by one printed path. On Winter, the river also divides forests as paths do.\n**Daylight:** **Move:** Exhaust one boot, plus **one extra boot** if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction (also for forced moves). Ignore rule. **Cannot enter a forest with this action; from a forest you may move only to an adjacent clearing.**\n**Evening:** If in forest, **Rest**: return all damaged items to Satchel and flip them face up; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if able. This does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. **Always draw**, even after forest Rest: one card plus one per face-up coins on track.','Refresh first counts tea already face up on Refresh track and flips two exhausted items face up per tea, then three more; tea refreshed now adds no refresh, and refreshing does not repair damage. Optional Slip moves to an adjacent clearing or forest free of boots, even into hostile warriors, and ignores effects preventing movement out of a clearing. Forest adjacency uses clearings touching without crossing printed paths and forests separated by one path; Winter rivers divide forests too. Normal Daylight Move costs one boot plus one extra if destination has warriors from any Hostile faction, ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest can go only to adjacent clearing. In Evening, forest Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel face up and puts ready tea/coins/bags on tracks if able; it does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Always draw one card plus one per face-up track coin, including after Rest.'),
('Q18','Vagabond — Daylight actions','**Explore:** Exhaust torch in ruin\'s clearing. Take one hidden item face up into Satchel or track; score one VP if an item taken. Remove ruin when its last item is taken, freeing the building slot.\n**Quest (matching clearing only):** Choose a face-up quest matching clearing; exhaust its **two listed items**, put quest in play area completed. Choose either VP equal to matching completed quests **including this one**, or draw two cards. Draw replacement quest into public display. No cards are spent to pay a quest.\n**Repair:** Exhaust hammer; move one damaged item to Satchel **keeping current face**. Ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if space.','Explore by exhausting a torch in a ruin’s clearing; take one hidden item face up into Satchel or track and score 1 VP if an item was taken. Removing the last ruin item removes the ruin and frees its slot. Quest requires a face-up quest matching your clearing; exhaust its two listed items, complete it, then choose VP equal to matching completed quests including this quest, or draw two cards; replace the displayed quest. No cards pay quests. Repair exhausts a hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel without changing its face; ready tea, coins, and bags move to tracks if space.'),
('Q19','Vagabond — Relationships / Strike / Hostile','**Strike:** Exhaust crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in clearing. Only if that enemy has no warriors there may you remove another of its faction pieces instead. Check hostility. Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.\n**Hostile:** Removing **one** warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately moves marker to Hostile (except allied battle-loss rule above). **Infamy:** During battle on your own turn, score **one extra VP per hostile piece removed**, except warrior that first made faction Hostile. **Each hostile building/token removed in battle on your turn normally scores two VP: one removal VP plus one Infamy. A hostile warrior scores one Infamy, except the warrior that first caused Hostile status.** Infamy depends on whose turn it is, rather than which side attacks: no Infamy on another player\'s turn, and none from Strike. Hostile status requires extra boot for moves into hostile warriors, not merely buildings/tokens.\n- Aid cannot move marker out of Hostile; it can still obtain a crafted item.','A faction becomes Hostile immediately when Vagabond removes one of its non-Hostile warriors, subject to the special Allied battle-loss rule. On Vagabond’s own turn, battle removal of hostile pieces earns 1 extra VP per hostile piece except the warrior that first caused Hostile status. A hostile building/token gives ordinary 1 VP plus 1 Infamy (2 total); a hostile warrior gives Infamy only, except the triggering warrior. Infamy is turn-based, not dependent on attacking: none on another player’s turn or from Strike. Aid cannot end Hostility, though it may still obtain a crafted item. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior; only if that faction has no warriors in the clearing can Strike remove another piece. It is not battle and earns no Infamy.'),
('Q20','Vagabond coalition','**Vagabond coalition (9.2.8):** Cannot activate normal dominance win. With **four or more players**, during own Daylight at **at least 10 VP**, activate dominance to coalition with another player **not already in coalition**, whose VP is lowest among players other than you (choose among ties). Put your score marker on partner\'s faction board and stop scoring. If partner wins, you also win, including if partner wins through dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition does not by itself grant Allied relationship powers.','Vagabond cannot activate normal dominance. With at least four players, in own Daylight at 10+ VP, activate dominance to coalition with a player not already in a coalition who has the lowest VP among players other than Vagabond (choose among ties). Put your score marker on that faction board and stop scoring. If partner wins by any means, including dominance, Vagabond wins too. Coalition partners are not enemies. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent; coalition alone does not grant Allied powers.'),
('Q21','Special Rules & Edge Cases — Precedence','**Precedence:** Card overrides Law; Law overrides Learning to Play. Follow general and faction rules together when possible; if incompatible, faction rule wins. **Cannot is absolute** unless explicitly overridden. (1.1.)','Cards override Law, Law overrides Learning to Play, and a faction rule wins over an incompatible general rule. Follow rules together when possible. “Cannot” is absolute unless an effect explicitly overrides it.'),
('Q22','Turn Structure','Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions. An action, ability or persistent effect cannot be interrupted unless an effect explicitly permits it; a Marquise March\'s two moves are one compound action. If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. For battle effects at the same timing, attacker chooses their order.','When simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player whose turn it is chooses. A Marquise March is one compound action, so it cannot be interrupted between its two moves to spend a bird or take another action. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions.'),
('Q23','Turn Structure','Take turns clockwise: **Birdsong → Daylight → Evening**. “At start” effects precede all other phase effects; “at end” effects follow everything else in that phase, before next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions.','“At start” effects occur before every other effect in that phase. “At end” effects occur after everything else in that phase and before the next phase. The turn’s phases are Birdsong, Daylight, Evening. When the last step of a turn begins, no further actions are allowed except actions explicitly permitted at the end of Evening/turn.'),
('Q24','Special Rules & Edge Cases — Cards','Hand size is public, contents private: reveal/show only if explicitly instructed. Face-up piles may be searched/inspected; deck cannot. Agreements are non-binding; cards may be transferred only as instructed; actions require no consent.','Hand size is public but hand contents are private and may be revealed only when instructed. Face-up piles can be searched; the deck cannot. Deals are non-binding; cards transfer only as instructed, and actions do not require consent.'),
('Q25','Special Rules & Edge Cases — Cards','Draw from shared deck top; when deck empties, immediately shuffle discard into new deck. **Cards:** Birds substitute for any non-bird suit, even for multiple same-suit payments. **If prompted to give or discard cards of a non-bird suit, you must treat your birds as that suit**; the instruction determines how many cards to give or discard. **Only a bird card can pay an explicit bird-card requirement; fox, rabbit and mouse cards cannot pay it.**','Draw from the deck top; as soon as it empties, shuffle the discard pile into a new deck. A bird substitutes for any non-bird suit, including multiple same-suit payments. When told to give/discard non-bird cards, birds count as that suit and the instruction determines number. An explicit bird-card cost can be paid only by a bird card.'),
('Q26','Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle','Pieces are finite: no proxies. When an instruction cannot place/take/remove all prompted pieces, **you must do the maximum possible and cannot voluntarily do fewer**; this never waives costs or prerequisites, nor the Eyrie\'s obligation to complete Decree actions.','Pieces are finite and cannot be proxied. If unable to place all prompted pieces, place as many as possible and do not voluntarily place fewer. A shortage does not waive costs or prerequisites and does not remove the Eyrie’s duty to complete a Decree action (failure causes Turmoil).'),
('Q27','Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle','Removed faction pieces normally return to supply; tracked pieces return to the **rightmost empty track space**. Placement normally takes pieces from supply, or leftmost on a track. Items removed from the game are removed permanently. ... For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects.','Pieces are normally placed from supply or the leftmost track position; removed pieces return to supply or the rightmost empty track space. Removed items are permanently removed. If pieces are removed simultaneously, remove all of them before resolving effects triggered by removal.'),
('Q28','Special Rules & Edge Cases — Force','**Force:** Resolve forced actions as if affected player chose them, retaining their abilities and restrictions. A player forced to battle makes its battle decisions.','Resolve a forced action as though the affected player chose it, with that player’s abilities and restrictions. A player forced to battle makes the battle decisions.'),
('Q29','Special Rules & Edge Cases — Place/remove/replace','**Place/remove/replace:** Place normally from supply/leftmost track; remove normally to supply/rightmost **empty** track space, items permanently. Replace requires both removal and placement possible; the keep\'s placement ban cannot be bypassed by replacing an enemy piece. Swap ignores move/place restrictions.','Replacement requires both removal and placement to be possible; it cannot bypass the Keep’s ban on placing pieces in its clearing. A swap ignores movement and placement restrictions.'),
('Q30','Scoring / Victory Conditions — 30 VP','If multiple reach 30 simultaneously, tied player closest clockwise to current player wins, including current player.','If multiple players reach 30 VP simultaneously, the tied player closest clockwise to the current player wins; the current player is included in this ordering.'),
('Q31','Overview / Vagabond — Slip','Fall has no special rules; on Winter, the river divides forests just as printed paths do. Rivers are otherwise not paths. **Forest adjacency for Slip:** a forest is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path, and to forests separated by one printed path. On Winter, the river also divides forests as paths do.','Fall has no special rules. For Slip, a forest is adjacent to clearings that touch it without crossing a printed path and to forests separated by one printed path. On Winter, the river divides forests like paths do; rivers otherwise are not paths.'),
('Q32','Setup — Marquise setup','**Marquise setup (6.3):** Supply 25 warriors and 8 wood. Put keep in any corner (starting clearing). Put one warrior in every clearing except the diagonally opposite corner. Place one sawmill, workshop and recruiter among the keep clearing and adjacent clearings, in any combination respecting slots. Put the remaining five buildings of each type on their tracks from right to left, leaving leftmost space empty.','Take 25 warriors and 8 wood. Put the Keep in any corner; put one warrior in every clearing except the diagonally opposite corner. Place one sawmill, workshop, and recruiter among the Keep clearing and adjacent clearings, in any arrangement allowed by slots. Put the remaining five buildings of each type on the tracks right-to-left, leaving the leftmost position empty.'),
('Q33','Setup — Eyrie setup','**Eyrie setup (7.3):** Supply 20 warriors. Put one roost and six warriors in a corner that is not another player\'s starting corner, diagonally opposite a starting corner if possible. Choose a leader; keep others face up nearby. Tuck the two bird Loyal Viziers into the columns listed on that leader. Fill roost track with the other six roosts from right to left.','Take 20 warriors. Put one roost and six warriors in a corner that is not another player’s starting corner, diagonally opposite a starting corner if possible. Choose a leader; leave others face up nearby. Tuck both bird Loyal Viziers into the columns listed for that leader. Put the other six roosts on the track from right to left.'),
('Q34','Setup — Alliance setup','**Alliance setup (8.3):** Supply 10 warriors. Put the three bases in their matching board spaces and ten sympathy on its track. Draw **three additional cards** face down into Supporters; these are separate from your three-card hand.
